title: Prematurity, Early Vascular Aging and Cardiorespiratory Fitness (PrEVAFit) – The impact of preterm birth and physical fitness on vascular health in children and adolescents.
summary:
Children born preterm have a significantly higher risk of suffering from cardiovascular diseases later in life. The reason for this is that their blood vessels are forced to continue maturing outside the womb during a very early and sensitive developmental phase. This can lead to a more rapid aging of the blood vessels than in children born term. While regular exercise and good physical fitness can positively influence vascular health, it remains unclear to what extent these factors can mitigate the increased cardiovascular risk in preterm-born individuals. Furthermore, the mechanisms underlying the positive effects of physical activity on the blood vessels of preterm-born individuals are not yet fully understood.
Consequently, the PrEVAFit study investigates the relationship between prematurity, vascular health, and physical activity / fitness.
The study includes 60 neonates born between 28+0 and 41+6 weeks of gestation, examined at a corrected age of 40 gestational weeks, and 60 adolescents born between 28+0 and 41+6 weeks of gestation at the age of 10 to 17. Data collection includes one blood sample, cheek swab, saliva sample (adolescents only), and stool samples (collected once from adolescents, twice from neonates at 3 days and 3 months of age). For the adolescent group, a cardiovascular risk profile, a lifestyle score, and a clinical profile of vascular health will be established, alongside assessments of cardiovascular and motor fitness. Additionally, vascular responsiveness to exercise will be examined during a single bout of high-intensity endurance exercise. This will provide insights into the "trainability" of vascular health in the context of preterm birth.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Neonates: Informed consent from at least one parent / legal guardian.

Adolescents: Age-appropriate information and consent from the child, as well as informed consent from at least one parent/legal guardian.
Exclusion criteria:
Neonates: Relevant anatomical malformations (especially cerebral, cardiac, and musculoskeletal); pulmonary hypertension; oxygen therapy; catecholamine-dependent circulatory depression; acute neurological disease (Grade IV intracranial hemorrhage, epilepsy); status post (S/P) severe necrotizing enterocolitis with intestinal resection.

Adolescents: Status post oncological disease involving chemotherapy or radiotherapy; symptomatic congenital heart defect or one currently requiring treatment; cerebral palsy; epilepsy; chronic eye disease (glaucoma); disease-related limitation of maximal physical exertion (e.g., pulmonary hypertension, acute injuries, motor disorders, or relevant mobility restrictions); inability to follow specific instructions (e.g., documented severe cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorder); acute mental/psychiatric illness requiring pharmacological treatment (e.g., schizophrenia, depression).
